key_insight: A general-purpose LLM (GPT-4o) can help draft case-series causality assessments for pharmacovigilance, with prompt design strongly affecting output quality.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLMs may speed up early signal assessment work by providing a structured starting point for human reviewers, rather than replacing expert judgment.
method: GPT-4o assessed causality for five drug/adverse-event combinations using Bradford Hill-style viewpoints adapted for case series.
The combinations included different drugs/vaccines, event types, and case-series sizes; one combination was a negative control.
Prompts were iteratively refined on one case, then applied to all combinations and evaluated by human annotators.
evidence_signal: Annotators agreed with 79–92% of the model’s output sentences, and 15 of 23 key signal segments were reflected in the LLM output for the recall check.
watch_item: The model can misread complex report details, so its outputs need expert review and careful prompt design before use in real pharmacovigilance workflows.
paper_title: AI as a signal assessor - Can a Large Language Model perform causality assessment on a case series?
